acceptanceCriteria: A synthetic fixture with a string enum reached through a barrel binds its injected state names; the test fails on base.
An ambiguous barrel (two candidate exports) stays unresolved and reports the reason.
A .constant('X', T) that does not bind produces a diagnostic naming the reason.
No private adopter names appear in fixtures or docs; the spec gets proposed requirements.
body: GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#705, a follow-up to #685 (V1-1027, AMAP-V0-021..023), on main-02e8457. The object-literal table case works (11 to 57 screens). It fails when the injected constant table is a TypeScript string enum whose members all have literal initializers, and when it reaches the registering file through a directory or barrel import (./routes, then index.ts, then export * from ./routes.constants). The build exits 0 with no diagnostic explaining why .constant('StateConstants', RoutesConstants) did not bind. The asks: treat all-literal string enums as name tables; follow one level of export * or export { X } from through an in-scope index.ts, failing closed when ambiguous; emit a diagnostic naming why an in-scope .constant binding did not resolve.
title: GitHub #705: appmap di_constants should read all-literal TS string enums and follow one barrel re-export level, with a no-bind diagnostic
